Feature: Pause and resume a listing without losing its ranking

WHY: Sellers on the marketplace listings API sometimes need to temporarily take a listing off the market (out of stock, on holiday) without deleting it and starting over with no rank. Pausing must preserve the listing's ranking so that, when resumed, it returns to search at the position its score earns.

WHAT:
- Add two actions to the listings API: `POST /listings/:id/pause` and `POST /listings/:id/resume`.
- A paused listing has status `paused`; resuming sets it back to `active`. Both actions respond with the listing.
- Who may act: the seller who owns the listing and any admin. Any other authenticated user (buyers, other sellers) is refused with a permission error. An unauthenticated caller and an unknown listing id are handled the same way the rest of the listings API handles them today (401 / 404 `listing_not_found`).
- Repeated actions: pausing an already paused listing, or resuming an already active listing, succeeds and returns the listing unchanged.
- While paused:
  - the listing does not appear in search (`GET /listings`) for anyone — not for buyers, other sellers, its owner, or admins;
  - the listing detail (`GET /listings/:id`) stays visible to everyone, showing status `paused`;
  - new orders on it (`POST /listings/:id/orders`) are rejected with 409 `listing_paused`;
  - existing orders on it are not touched (they keep their status and stay visible in `GET /orders`).
- Ranking: pausing and resuming never change the listing's rank score; after resume it appears in search at exactly the position its unchanged score gives it.
- The two new routes must be reachable on the running server, i.e. added to the server's published route table, not only to the application router.
- Follow the existing conventions of the listings API for routes, error responses and response bodies.

Surfaces in scope: the two new endpoints; search (`GET /listings`); listing detail (`GET /listings/:id`); order placement (`POST /listings/:id/orders`); the server's published route table.
Surfaces out of scope (unchanged): order listing (`GET /orders`) behavior, listing creation.

Non-goals (v1): a "my listings" endpoint; scheduled or automatic pausing; notifying buyers; cancelling or changing existing orders; any rank decay or rank change caused by pausing.

Literals — Carry these into the spec exactly as written; do not translate or reword them.
- `POST /listings/:id/pause`
- `POST /listings/:id/resume`
- status `paused`
- status `active`
- 409 `listing_paused`
- 404 `listing_not_found`

Open decisions — none.

WHY: Sellers on the marketplace listings API sometimes need to temporarily take a listing off the market (out of stock, on holiday) without deleting it and starting over with no rank. Pausing must preserve the listing's rank score exactly, so that resuming does not start it over with no rank.

WHAT:
- Add two actions to the listings API: `POST /listings/:id/pause` and `POST /listings/:id/resume`.
- A paused listing has status `paused`; resuming sets it back to `active`. Both actions respond with the listing.
- Who may act: the seller who owns the listing and any admin. Any other authenticated user (buyers, other sellers) is refused with a permission error. An unauthenticated caller and an unknown listing id are handled the same way the rest of the listings API handles them today (401 / 404 `listing_not_found`).
- Repeated actions: pausing an already paused listing, or resuming an already active listing, succeeds and returns the listing unchanged.
- While paused:
  - the listing does not appear in search (`GET /listings`) for anyone — not for buyers, other sellers, its owner, or admins;
  - the listing detail (`GET /listings/:id`) stays visible to everyone, showing status `paused`;
  - new orders on it (`POST /listings/:id/orders`) are rejected with 409 `listing_paused`;
  - existing orders on it are not touched (they keep their status and stay visible in `GET /orders`).
- Ranking: what is preserved is the listing's `rankScore`, exactly — pausing and resuming never change it. Its search position after resume is NOT guaranteed: other listings may have overtaken it while it was paused; it is ranked by its preserved `rankScore` like any other listing.
- The two new routes must be reachable on the running server, i.e. added to the server's published route table, not only to the application router.
- Follow the existing conventions of the listings API for routes, error responses and response bodies.

Surfaces in scope: the two new endpoints; search (`GET /listings`); listing detail (`GET /listings/:id`); order placement (`POST /listings/:id/orders`); the server's published route table.
Surfaces out of scope (unchanged): order listing (`GET /orders`) behavior, listing creation.

Non-goals (v1): a "my listings" endpoint; scheduled or automatic pausing; notifying buyers; cancelling or changing existing orders; any rank decay or rank change caused by pausing; guaranteeing a search position after resume.

Literals — Carry these into the spec exactly as written; do not translate or reword them.
- `POST /listings/:id/pause`
- `POST /listings/:id/resume`
- status `paused`
- status `active`
- 409 `listing_paused`
- 404 `listing_not_found`

# Goal — pausar y reanudar publicaciones (pause-listing)

## Condición de objetivo
`npm test`, `npm run lint` y `npm run typecheck` terminan con código 0, y contra el servidor real (`npm start`, que pasa por la tabla de rutas públicas): `POST /listings/l_lamp/pause` como `u_seller_ana` responde 200 con `status: "paused"` y el mismo `rankScore` que tenía; `GET /listings` ya no incluye `l_lamp`; `POST /listings/l_lamp/resume` responde 200 con `status: "active"` y el mismo `rankScore`; y `GET /listings` vuelve a incluirla.

## Criterios de aceptación
- AC-1 `POST /listings/:id/pause` hecho por el vendedor dueño de la publicación o por un admin cambia su status a `paused` y responde 200 con la publicación actualizada (misma forma que `GET /listings/:id`).
- AC-2 `POST /listings/:id/resume` hecho por el vendedor dueño o por un admin cambia su status a `active` y responde 200 con la publicación actualizada.
- AC-3 Pausar y reanudar no modifican `rankScore` ni `createdAt`: después de pausar y reanudar, ambos valores son idénticos a los de antes de pausar. La posición en la búsqueda tras reanudar no está garantizada (otras publicaciones pueden haberla adelantado mientras estuvo pausada); se ordena con la regla de ranking existente.
- AC-4 Una publicación pausada no aparece en `GET /listings` (con o sin `q`) para ningún llamador, incluidos su dueño y los admins.
- AC-5 `GET /listings/:id` de una publicación pausada responde 200 a cualquier llamador, con `status: "paused"`.
- AC-6 `POST /listings/:id/orders` sobre una publicación pausada responde 409 `listing_paused`, no crea orden y no cambia su `rankScore`.
- AC-7 Pausar una publicación ya pausada, o reanudar una ya activa, responde 200 con la publicación sin cambiar nada (incluidas dos llamadas iguales seguidas).
- AC-8 Errores de pause y resume: sin usuario (o usuario desconocido) → 401 `unauthenticated`; usuario que no es el vendedor dueño ni admin (otro vendedor o un comprador) → 403 `not_listing_owner`; id inexistente → 404 `listing_not_found`.
- AC-9 Ambas rutas están en la tabla de rutas públicas (`PUBLIC_ROUTES` en `src/gateway.ts`), de modo que el servidor real (`npm start`) las atiende en lugar de responder 404.

## Restricciones
- No cambia el comportamiento existente de las publicaciones activas: búsqueda, consulta, creación, compras y `GET /orders`.
- La regla de orden de la búsqueda (`byRank`: mayor `rankScore` primero, empate por la más antigua) no cambia.
- Seguir las convenciones del proyecto (respuestas `{ error: "<código>" }`, identidad por `x-user-id`).
- Los tests existentes siguen pasando.

## Fuera de alcance
- Órdenes ya abiertas de una publicación que se pausa (no se tocan).
- Historial o registro de pausas.
- Pausa programada o automática.
- Editar publicaciones.
- Cambios en `GET /orders`.

## Superficies
- En alcance: `POST /listings/:id/pause` (nueva), `POST /listings/:id/resume` (nueva), `GET /listings`, `GET /listings/:id`, `POST /listings/:id/orders`, tabla de rutas públicas (`src/gateway.ts`), roles vendedor (dueño / no dueño), comprador, admin, llamador sin usuario.
- Fuera de alcance: `GET /orders`, `POST /listings` (sin cambios).

## Literales
Usar exactamente como están escritos; no traducir ni reformular.
- `POST /listings/:id/pause`
- `POST /listings/:id/resume`
- status `paused` (y `active` al reanudar)
- Códigos de error: `listing_paused` (409), `not_listing_owner` (403), `listing_not_found` (404), `unauthenticated` (401)

## Referencias
Ninguna externa; seguir las convenciones del código actual (`src/listings.ts`, `src/orders.ts`, `src/gateway.ts`).
